findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache map without lock while builds can now write it concurrently
findings.body:
`BuildIndex` no longer holds `cacheMu` for its whole body; it now writes `b.cache[key]` under a short lock. `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu` at all.

In `searchSupport.init`, the watch goroutine is started (search.go:207) before `s.search.TotalDocs()` is called (search.go:216). `handleEvent` -> `getOrCreateIndex` -> `BuildIndex` can therefore write the map while `TotalDocs` is iterating it. Search requests can do the same once the server is up.

Concurrent map iteration and write is a fatal runtime error in Go and will crash the process. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same key
findings.body:
With the coarse lock gone, nothing stops two callers from building the same NamespacedResource at once. Callers include `getOrCreateIndex` from Search (including federated lookups) and from `handleEvent`, and the init workers. Each caller sees `GetIndex == nil` and calls `BuildIndex`.

For in-memory indexes, one fully built index silently replaces the other. Writes applied to the losing index by a concurrent watch event are lost, and the IndexTenants/IndexedKinds metrics are double counted.

For file-based indexes (`size > FileThreshold`), both callers run `bleve.New` on the same directory and the second fails. A per-key singleflight or lock is needed to keep the speedup without this race.

findings.title: Init worker goroutines race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed`
findings.body:
Inside `group.Go`, each goroutine assigns the outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments `totalBatchesIndexed` with no synchronization. Both are data races.

This PR's goal is to make these builds actually run in parallel by removing the backend lock, which makes the races far more likely to bite. One goroutine's error can be overwritten by another, and the reported count is unreliable.

The goroutine should use a local `err` and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Requests are no longer rejected after Stop
findings.body:
`Stop` still sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" / "service is stopped". Previously every handler called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returned that `initErr`, so requests were rejected after shutdown.

This PR removes those `Init` calls from all handlers. After `Stop`, Create/Read/List/Watch/etc. now run against a stopped backend instead of returning a clean error. `initErr` is effectively dead after construction.

Either keep a cheap stopped/initErr check in the handlers or remove the now-meaningless assignments.

findings.title: Context cancel leaked when Init fails in constructor
findings.body:
`NewResourceServer` creates `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` and then returns `nil, err` if `s.Init(ctx)` fails, without calling `cancel`.

Any goroutines or watchers started during partial initialization keep running. For example, the search watch goroutine may already be started if only `initWatcher` failed. They are never cancelled.

`cancel()` should be called on the error path.

findings.title: Postgres integration test skipped instead of fixed
findings.body:
The storage-server module test is now skipped for postgres in CI. This likely follows from the behaviour change to eager initialization in the constructor, which is exactly what the test exercises.

Skipping it removes coverage for eager init against postgres, the scenario the PR description itself asks reviewers to worry about. It should be fixed, or the root cause should be documented.
